requirements.title: A program has one main program and may have other program units or external entities
requirements.definition: A program shall consist of exactly one main program, plus any number of other kinds of program units, external procedures, and non-Fortran entities.

pending.exactly-one-fortran-main-program: Compile and run a source with one PROGRAM main plus a module and external subroutine; main initializes x=-1, calls the subroutine, and checks x==65.
pending.zero-or-more-other-program-units: Compile and run a source whose only Fortran program unit is PROGRAM main assigning and checking integer sentinel 66.
pending.two-fortran-main-programs-source-control: Diagnostic source contains PROGRAM p and PROGRAM q in the same Fortran program; repair removes only PROGRAM q and its END PROGRAM.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish distinct sentinels before the observed action, use exact integer or logical results, and avoid compiler-message wording or processor-dependent process status values.

requirements.title: The main program is Fortran-defined or non-Fortran-defined but not both
requirements.definition: The main program shall be defined by a Fortran main-program program-unit or by means other than Fortran, but not both.

pending.fortran-main-origin: Compile and run an ordinary Fortran PROGRAM main that calls a BIND(C) helper only as an auxiliary procedure and exits after checking sentinel 67.
pending.companion-main-origin: Build a mixed C/Fortran source where C main calls a BIND(C) Fortran subroutine that returns sentinel 68; no Fortran PROGRAM unit appears.
pending.both-main-origins-prohibited: Source-control negative combines the companion C main from the previous plan with an otherwise ordinary Fortran PROGRAM main; no portable mandatory diagnostic wording or link status is asserted.
